hints: Focus on the two carbons of the C=C double bond and what is attached to each one.
Remember geometric isomerism needs two different groups on the left C and two different groups on the right C, because the double bond cannot rotate.
Check each alkene for a C with two identical H atoms or two identical methyl groups, then pick the one where both ends are different.
walkthrough:
**Recall the rule for geometric isomerism**

Think of the C=C bond as locked in place with no rotation. For cis-trans isomers to exist, each carbon must hold two different groups.

Rule:
$$ \text{each C of C=C must have two different substituents} $$

**Inspect both ends of each double bond**

Look carefully at what is bonded to the left C and the right C. If either carbon has two H atoms, or two $\text{CH}_3$ groups, geometric isomerism is impossible.

Example to reject:
$$ \text{R}_2\text{C=CH}_2 \text{ cannot show geometric isomerism} $$

**Apply to the four alkenes**

Only $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CHCH}_3$ has different groups at both ends. Left C has $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2$ and $\text{H}$, right C has $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{H}$.

Structure:
$$ \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CHCH}_3 \text{ (pent-2-ene)} $$
So this alkene can exist as cis and trans forms.

options.A: Incorrect. This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CH}_2$. The right hand carbon has two H atoms, so swapping positions gives the same molecule. No cis-trans pair is possible.
options.B: Correct. This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH=CHCH}_3$ (pent-2-ene). Each C of the double bond carries two different groups, so cis (Z) and trans (E) isomers exist.
options.C: Incorrect. This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(CH}_3\text{)=CH}_2$. The right hand carbon has two H atoms ($\text{=CH}_2$), so both positions on that end are identical and no geometric isomerism occurs.
options.D: Incorrect. This is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=C(CH}_3\text{)}_2$. The right hand carbon has two identical $\text{CH}_3$ groups, so even though the left side is different, the molecule cannot have cis-trans isomers.
